chunks: Basair al-Darajat: Abdallah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Ruba'i, from al-Fadl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Allah has a knowledge which His angels, prophets, and messengers know. Behold! We too know it. And Allah has a knowledge which His angels, prophets, and messengers do not know.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the knowledge of angels and the knowledge of the Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Basa’ir al-Darajat* articulates the Shia doctrine of *al-Ilm al-Mutlaq* (absolute knowledge) of the Imams, distinguishing between the general divine knowledge accessible to prophets and the specific, esoteric knowledge (*al-Ilm al-Khass*) reserved for the Ahl al-Bayt. It underscores their unique epistemological status as inheritors of the Prophet’s complete wisdom, bridging the gap between the manifest (*zahir*) and the hidden (*batin*) aspects of revelation.

en.ammaar-muslim: 9. [9/-] Basair al-Darajat: Abdallah b. Ja’far from Muhammad b. Isa from Ibn Abi Umayr from Rib’i from al-Fudhayl from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام who said:
Allah has a knowledge which is known by His angels, prophets and messengers. Behold! We too do know it. Allah also has a knowledge which His angels, prophets and messengers do not know about.
